newsitem.title: POLAND: Sunny Warsaw awaits NATO entry party with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Sunny Warsaw awaits NATO entry party with Clinton.

text.p: Four days heavy rain ended in Warsaw on Wednesday just in time for a street party at which U.S. President Bill Clinton is expected to congratulate Poland on being invited to join NATO.
A five-hour event on the Warsaw Old Town's Castle Square on Thursday, featuring country, jazz and folk music of the two nations, will culminate in a 15-minute address by Clinton.
"We welcome you to NATO and congratulate you," is Clinton's message to Poles, U.S. ambassador Nicholas Rey told reporters.

Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary were invited to start negotiations on membership of the western miliary alliance on Tuesday at its Madrid summit, which Polish commentators called one of the most important moments in the last 300 years.

The Polish and U.S. organisers have been concerned that the party, expected to attract some 20,000 people, would be spoiled by heavy rains, which hit Poland taking lives of 12 people in flooding large areas of the south.
"Thank God for the sun," said the event's artistic director Jaroslaw Kilian.
Warsaw residents were collecting souvenir invitations to the party, which read "Join us. Be part of history."
"Sure I will come. I appreciate that President Clinton will personally be here," said Agata Nowak, a student.

Crowds will listen to music of Polish national composer Frederic Chopin, arranged in jazz-style, American pieces such as "Chattanooga choo choo," "The Pink Panther" by Henry Mancini and military marches.
"The event is to combine cultural and military tradition of the two nations," said its main director Wieslaw Dabrowski.

Clinton, scheduled to arrive in Warsaw at 13.00 local time, will hold plenary and private talks with President Kwasniewski, followed by the open-air address and an official dinner. He will leave for Romania on Friday morning.
